definitions.explanation: The body of law governing commercial transactions and businesses; in Japan, one of the Six Codes. Also used loosely to mean a particular way of doing business.

examples.japanese: {商法|しょうほう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{改正|かいせい}→改正：00446_kaisei⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧。
⟦{会社|かいしゃ}→会社：00607_kaisha⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{設立|せつりつ}→設立：14171_setsuritsu⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{商法|しょうほう}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{基|もと}づいて→基づく：02315_motozuku⟧⟦{行|おこな}われる→行う：01238_okonau⟧。
examples.english: The establishment of a company is carried out based on the commercial code.

examples.japanese: ⟦{強引|ごういん}→強引：04156_gouin⟧な⟦{勧誘|かんゆう}→勧誘：16850_kanyuu⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧{悪徳|あくとく}{商法|しょうほう}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{注意|ちゅうい}→注意：01464_chuui⟧⟦して→する：00392_suru⟧⟦ください→ください：02899_kudasai⟧。
examples.english: Please be careful of unscrupulous business practices that use forceful solicitation.

notes:
Composed of ⟦{商|しょう}→商：26727_shou⟧ (commerce) + ⟦{法|ほう}→法：13620_hou⟧ (law). As one of the Six Codes, it governs merchants, companies, and commercial transactions.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {商法|しょうほう}⟦{改正|かいせい}→改正：00446_kaisei⟧: revision of the commercial code
- {会社法|かいしゃほう}: the Companies Act — split off from the commercial code in 2005
- {悪徳|あくとく}{商法|しょうほう}: unscrupulous / fraudulent business practices

USAGE:
Beyond the statute, {商法|しょうほう} is often used in the sense of a "way of doing business," especially in the fixed phrase {悪徳|あくとく}{商法|しょうほう} (shady sales tactics).
